evidence: REVIEWED — 3 findings, all in this ticket's own code, all fixed and re-verified. Full write-up at .autodev/evidence/T-2/review.md. (1) SECURITY, confirmed exploit not theory: the SPA fallback did 'dist / full_path' with no containment check, so curl --path-as-is on /../../.env returned 200 with bytes sha256-identical to the real .env carrying non-empty TMDB_API_KEY and PEXELS_API_KEY. Browsers normalise '..' so every browser test passed; non-browser clients do not. Loopback-only and nothing left the machine, so no rotation needed. Fixed by resolving the candidate and requiring dist_root containment (dist_root resolved once, so symlinks cannot widen it); re-tested 5 traversal payloads, all now return the SPA shell, while hashed CSS, /api/health and / are unaffected. (2) bootstrap() leaked a connection per call because 'with sqlite3.connect()' manages the transaction, not the connection; fixed with try/finally close, re-verified by counting /proc/self/fd across 50 bootstraps — 4 to 4, zero leaked. (3) WAL sidecars (-wal/-shm) hold uncheckpointed committed rows but were protected only by the data/ rule, so a relocated MEDIA_LIST_DB would thin the privacy boundary; added explicit ignores, re-verified with git check-ignore. Three further items considered and deliberately left with reasons recorded: per-call connections, import-time bootstrap, and start.sh's grep/cut .env read.

evidence: LOCATE at .autodev/locates/T-3.md. Maps exactly what T-2 already provides so this ticket adds no plumbing it does not need: config already types the three credentials as str|None (AC7's degrade is a truthiness check), the /api router is already included ahead of the SPA catch-all, /art is already mounted on art_dir so AC6 only needs the writing half, and the schema already models source/source_id/nullable imdb_id/detail so no migration is required. Carries forward T-2's handed-on regression: adding routes means re-running the traversal check at verify. Upstream facts were confirmed by reading the APIs rather than recalled: search/multi carries origin_country on tv but original_language on movies (which is WHY AC2's rule is an OR); external_ids is a separate call so AC4's second round trip is by necessity; TMDB returns path fragments not URLs; AniList has no id mapping from TMDB so anime enrichment is a fuzzy title match; IGDB uses apicalypse POST bodies and templated cover image_ids. Three risks recorded: fuzzy AniList matches must decorate and never replace a TMDB title; images must NOT be downloaded during search because search is typed-into; and the token cache file needs 0600 and must stay inside gitignored data/.

evidence: PLAN at .autodev/plans/T-3.md: 6 steps, each mapped to the ACs it satisfies. Records one deliberate reading of the spec rather than resolving it silently — AC6 says the response never hands the frontend a remote URL, but downloading artwork during a typed-into search would pull megabytes per keystroke, so the cache is filled at details/add time and the candidate LIST carries remote URLs. That reading is written down for review to accept or reject. Also records: AniList decorates and may never change title/year/kind (locate risk 1), and each source is awaited independently so one dying returns the other's results plus a named error rather than an empty list that reads as 'no matches'.

evidence: REVIEWED — 2 findings, both in this ticket's own code, both fixed and re-verified; written up in .autodev/evidence/T-3/build-and-review.md. (1) SILENT WRONG ANSWER: tmdb.details() guessed between the movie and tv namespaces when the caller gave no media_type. TMDB ids are namespace-scoped, so this did not fail — it returned a different plausible title: /api/details/tmdb/30991 returned 'The Curse of the Living Corpse' (1964) instead of Cowboy Bebop, and /api/details/tmdb/550 with a tv hint returned 'Till Death Us Do Part' instead of Fight Club. Wrong title, wrong poster, wrong IMDb id, and T-4 would have persisted it. Fixed to refuse rather than guess; the resulting obligation on T-4 (persist media_type with any stored TMDB title) is recorded in kb/CURRENT-WORK.md so it survives the ticket boundary. (2) Every SourceError was wrapped as 502, so a caller mistake read as an upstream outage; fixed to pass 400/404 through while 401/429/5xx still become 502 — re-verified: missing media_type 400, bad id 404, unknown source 404, good request 200. T-2's handed-forward traversal regression re-run because this ticket added routes: ../../.env and ../../.git/config both return the SPA shell with 0 secrets.
